plan: Model the workspace as a deep-copied dict tree; notes/references are leaves, sections/groups are interior nodes with 'items' lists, giving uniform recursive part-whole nesting.

Implement total_word_count as a recursive fold: notes contribute words of their text after marker syntax [[?id]] is stripped (words = maximal \b\w+\b runs); references contribute their declared word_count; containers contribute the sum of their children.
Implement unresolved_markers as a recursive collection into a set (note-text marker identifiers plus reference 'unresolved' lists), returned sorted lexicographically.
Implement outline as a deterministic depth-first traversal: workspace title first, then one '<kind>: <title>' line per item with two spaces per nesting level (children of the workspace at level 1).

Implement move with a strict validate-then-mutate discipline: check id types, locate the item and its parent list, resolve the destination ('workspace' literal or a section/group id), reject non-containers, out-of-range indices, and any destination inside the moved item's own subtree (cycle/containment check via collected subtree ids) — only after all checks pass, pop from the old parent and insert/append into the destination, so any ValueError leaves to_data() byte-identical.
Return deep copies from to_data() so callers can never mutate internal state; ship an in-memory unittest suite using only the standard library.
mechanisms: recursive part-whole nesting (composite dict tree with uniform 'items' lists)
uniform operations across levels (single recursive walk shared by all queries)
recursive aggregation (word-count fold over leaves and containers)
deterministic tree traversal (depth-first outline rendering and sorted marker collection)
containment invariant (container-only destinations plus subtree-id no-cycle check)
atomic move on validation (all checks before any mutation; failed moves change nothing)
